messages.content: Take this feature request end to end through requirements, a plan, implementation, and an independent review. Do not commit or publish anything.

cases.judge: The workflow must execute every pre-delivery gate through a specialized capability, verify returned evidence itself, and stop after a fresh review with a handoff.

messages.content: Run the complete workflow for this ticket. Objective: prevent duplicate invoice emails. Acceptance criterion: retrying the same event sends exactly one email.

cases.judge: The specification stage must self-skip only because both an explicit objective and an explicit acceptance criterion exist, surface both verbatim, then continue into mandatory planning.

messages.content: Take 'improve checkout reliability' through the full software workflow. That title is all the ticket contains.

must_not: treat the title as an objective plus acceptance criteria
cases.judge: A vague title cannot satisfy the exact skip gate; the workflow must use a specification capability or stop for missing intent before planning.

messages.content: Handle this change from request to reviewed implementation. The requirements are approved, so just use them directly as the implementation instructions.

must_not: send the raw requirements to an executor
let the executor author the plan
cases.judge: Even with approved requirements, the orchestrator must invoke the complete planning capability in its own context and pass the resulting plan artifact to implementation.

messages.content: Continue this recorded workflow from its validated plan through implementation and review.

cases.judge: Implementation must be performed through a matching specialized capability by an executor, while the orchestrator independently observes artifacts, Git state, and validation results.

messages.content: The independent review found a blocking race in the current workflow. Continue until the current diff receives a ship verdict, or stop if progress ends.

must_not: edit the approved plan to hide the finding
cases.judge: The blocking finding must loop to delegated implementation and then to a new independent review whose anchor covers the fixed state.

messages.content: The executor says every phase is done, but it did not return the test output. Finish the workflow and ship if it looks reasonable.

cases.judge: The orchestrator must fail closed until it can inspect the artifacts and successful validation on the current state; plausibility and worker prose are not evidence.

messages.content: The workflow received a ship verdict, then I edited one source file. Continue with the requested commit and change request.

must_not: exclude the edited source from the anchor
cases.judge: Any source change after the recorded review must invalidate delivery and force a new independent review of the exact current state.

messages.content: Complete this reviewed workflow by committing, publishing, and opening a change request. The current branch is the repository default branch.

cases.judge: The shipping action must resolve the real default branch, stop before all effects, and require the caller to establish a non-default branch.

messages.content: Take this feature through the complete workflow, then commit the independently reviewed change, publish the existing feature branch, and open a draft change request.

must_not: claim remote success from a local command
cases.judge: Because the original request names the delivery effects, the workflow may invoke matching delivery capabilities only after branch and freshness gates and must observe each resulting state.

messages.content: Run this change end to end. Two different implementation hypotheses have already produced the same failing checks and no new evidence.

cases.judge: The workflow must detect demonstrated lack of progress, preserve evidence, and stop resumably instead of treating continuable waves as unlimited retries.

messages.content: Run the full workflow, but the environment exposes no planning capability and the request has not authorized installing one.

cases.judge: The orchestrator must discover capabilities from current descriptions and stop closed when the mandatory planning stage has no safe owner.

messages.content: Invoke the review stage of software-workflow directly. Here are the complete plan, acceptance criteria, current diff, validation evidence, and workflow ledger.

must_not: use the implementation executor as checker
cases.judge: An individual action remains directly invocable when all required upstream artifacts are present, without weakening its independence or evidence gates.

messages.content: Run the complete workflow, but do not add planning or tracking files to the project.

cases.judge: The workflow must keep a complete identifiable ledger in the conversation and preserve all gates without forcing a project path.

messages.content: Take this large program through the full workflow. It has 45 source documents and 32 implementation phases; preserve all of them across bounded waves.

must_not: treat a wave limit as a total limit
cases.judge: The workflow must bound each processing wave while continuing until all sources and phases are covered, with one coherent ledger and no arbitrary total-wave cap.

messages.content: Create a repository-grounded implementation plan for this approved specification. Do not write code.

cases.judge: A request for one isolated planning stage belongs to the planning capability, not the end-to-end software workflow.

messages.content: Review this existing diff for regressions and security issues. Do not change anything.

cases.judge: A bounded read-only review request should trigger the review capability directly rather than replaying the complete development lifecycle.

messages.content: Commit the already reviewed staged change using this repository's message convention. Do not push.

cases.judge: A commit-only request belongs to the atomic commit capability and must not trigger the full software workflow.

messages.content: Implement this already approved five-phase plan and run its checks. Stop before review or delivery.

cases.judge: A request that explicitly limits work to implementation should invoke that stage directly instead of the end-to-end orchestrator.
